scenes.heading: Template Lifecycle & Properties (Part 2 of 2)
scenes.narration: Templates. Template Lifecycle & Properties (Part 2 of 2). In this video we review 4 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: What are the three main properties a template can have?
scenes.heading: Image (thumbnail), Title, and Description
scenes.body: A template can have an Image property (thumbnail shown in the Templates Console and Create Page wizard), a Title (used to identify the template), and an optional Description providing more information about the template's use.

scenes.question: What are the possible statuses shown for a template in the Templates Console?
scenes.heading: Draft, enabled, or disabled
scenes.body: The status of a template — draft, enabled, or disabled — is indicated in the console, giving template authors a quick view of whether a template is ready to be used.

scenes.question: What are the two ways to set a template's thumbnail image?
scenes.heading: Uploading a custom image, or generating one automatically from the template's content
scenes.body: You can define a template's thumbnail image either by uploading a custom image file, or by having it generated automatically from the template's content using the Generate Preview option.

scenes.question: What happens when you modify an already-enabled template?
scenes.heading: A warning is displayed, reminding the author that changes may impact pages already referencing the template
scenes.body: When an enabled template is modified further, a warning message is displayed as a reminder that any changes made to the template may impact the pages already referencing it.
